exec: A maintenance-related disruption to a top-secret government network; critical communications reportedly stayed available.
impact: The agency staggered staff arrivals and logins and sent non-essential staff a Code Gray notice; a source said classified work continued unimpeded.
plain: The classified internal network used by US National Security Agency staff went down or ran intermittently on November 17. The agency says routine scheduled maintenance caused it; there is no evidence of a cyberattack.

sources.name: New Turkish Post (Arabic): outage enters third day

summary: CNN reported, citing six people, that NSA Net went down on November 17; other sources say it was intermittent. The NSA cites degradation during scheduled routine maintenance, and DNI Jay Clayton blamed a PHP patch and said there is no evidence of a cyberattack. On November 18 The Record, citing a source, said the network was working but staff arrivals and logins were still staggered, with full restoration possibly a day or two away. New Turkish Post, relaying NBC, CNN and Fox, said on 20 November the outage had entered a third day and repairs were slower than expected, per an official cited by CNN.
title: NSA's classified internal network NSA Net goes down

validation.note: Agency statement plus several outlets; extent of the outage is described differently by different sources. The Record's second-day report (read) cites one unnamed source for the network working and restoration taking a day or two.

review.note: Compared with The Record (both days) and WRAL: NSA maintenance statement, DNI PHP patch, no evidence of cyberattack, intermittent service, staggered logins, Code Gray, 1-2 days restoration; outage not called an attack
